extracted.intended_audience: community and non-transient non-community public water system operators, state primacy agencies, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements under 40 CFR part 141 Subpart H (monitoring/reporting) and Subpart I (lead and copper control) describing monitoring, reporting, treatment technique, action levels, 90th-percentile calculation, corrosion control treatment steps, recycle provisions, and associated recordkeeping and deadlines for public water systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity sampling frequency reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: State may reduce turbidity sampling frequency to once per day for systems using slow sand filtration or filtration other than conventional, direct filtration, or diatomaceous earth filtration if the State determines less frequent monitoring is sufficient; for systems serving 500 or fewer persons, State may reduce turbidity sampling to once per day regardless of filtration type if State determines less frequent monitoring is sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an allowance by the State based on a determination that once-per-day monitoring is sufficient to indicate effective filtration performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual disinfectant continuous monitoring and grab-sample alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: Residual disinfectant concentration of water entering the distribution system must be monitored continuously and the lowest value recorded each day; if continuous monitoring equipment fails, grab sampling every 4 hours may be used for up to 5 working days following equipment failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems serving 3,300 or fewer persons may use grab sampling in lieu of continuous monitoring on an ongoing basis at prescribed daily frequencies by system size (≤500: 1 sample/day; 501–1,000: 2 samples/day; 1,001–2,500: 3 samples/day; 2,501–3,300: 4 samples/day). The day's samples cannot be taken at the same time. Sampling intervals are subject to State review and approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when residual disinfectant < 0.2 mg/L under grab-sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: If at any time the residual disinfectant concentration falls below 0.2 mg/L in a system using grab sampling in lieu of continuous monitoring, the system must take a grab sample every 4 hours until the residual disinfectant concentration is equal to or greater than 0.2 mg/L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued intensified sampling every 4 hours is required until the residual is restored to ≥0.2 mg/L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfectant residual sampling points and alternatives (timing/locations/HPC substitution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until March 31, 2016 residual disinfectant concentration must be measured at the same points and times as total coliforms sampled (§141.21). Beginning April 1, 2016 residual disinfectant must be measured at least at the same points/times as total coliforms as specified in §§141.854–141.858. State may allow alternate points if more representative of treated (disinfected) water quality. Heterotrophic plate count (HPC) may be measured in lieu of residual disinfectant concentration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the State determines a system cannot transport/analyze HPC under required time/temperature conditions and the system is providing adequate disinfection, the requirement to measure at the same points/times does not apply to that system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly source water quality reporting content (unfiltered/surface water/no filtration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public water system using a surface water source and not providing filtration must report monthly to the State source water quality information within 10 days after the end of each month the system serves water to the public (or as otherwise phased if State has required filtration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required reported items include: cumulative number of months reported; number of fecal and/or total coliform samples and dates (if both monitored, only fecal coliforms reported); number of samples with ≤20/100 ml fecal coliforms and/or ≤100/100 ml total coliforms; cumulative number of such samples during previous six months; percentage meeting those thresholds over previous six months; maximum turbidity measured during the month and dates/notifications for any measurements >5 NTU; dates and cumulative number of turbidity >5 NTU events for first 12 months and thereafter for prior 12 months; dates and cumulative number of turbidity >5 NTU events for first 120 months and thereafter for prior 120 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly disinfection reporting content
rubrics_metrics.description: Disinfection information specified in §141.74(b)/(c) must be reported to the State within 10 days after the end of each month the system serves water to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must include: daily lowest residual disinfectant concentration (mg/L) entering distribution; date/duration of each period residual <0.2 mg/L and date State was notified; daily residual concentration(s) and disinfectant contact time(s) used for CT calculations; if chlorine used, daily pH of disinfected water following each chlorine disinfection point; daily water temperature (°C) after each disinfection point; daily CTcalc and CTcalc/CT99.9 values for each measurement/sequence and the sum of CTcalc/CT99.9 before or at the first customer; daily determination whether disinfection achieves adequate Giardia cyst and virus inactivation (i.e., CTcalc/CT99.9 ≥ 1.0 or other State-determined indicators); and distribution-system sample metadata in conjunction with total coliform monitoring (counts of instances in which residual is measured/not measured, HPC measured, residual detected/not detected, HPC >500/ml, and the value “V” computed from specified a–e components). Systems may be exempt from some distribution-sample reporting if State determines system cannot meet HPC transport/analysis conditions and is providing adequate disinfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual watershed control and on-site inspection reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than ten days after the end of each Federal fiscal year (Sept 30), each system must provide to the State a report summarizing compliance with watershed control program requirements (§141.71(b)(2)) and a report on the on-site inspection conducted that year pursuant to §141.71(b)(3), unless the on-site inspection was conducted by the State (in which case the State must provide its report to the system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely annual summaries and inspection reports are required for State review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate reporting/consultation requirements for outbreaks and exceedances
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report certain events promptly: upon discovering a potential waterborne disease outbreak attributable to the system, report to the State as soon as possible but no later than end of next business day; if turbidity exceeds 5 NTU, consult with the primacy agency as soon as practical but no later than 24 hours after the exceedance is known (per public notification §141.203(b)(3)); if residual falls below 0.2 mg/L in water entering distribution, notify the State as soon as possible but no later than end of next business day and notify by end of next business day whether residual was restored to ≥0.2 mg/L within 4 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory notification timeframes tied to public-notification and State consultation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly filtered-water turbidity reporting (systems with filtration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public water systems using surface water or GWUDI and providing filtration must report monthly turbidity information within 10 days after the end of each month the system serves water to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported items include total number of filtered-water turbidity measurements taken during the month; number and percentage of measurements ≤ the turbidity limits in §141.73 for the filtration technology used; date and value of any monthly turbidity measurements that exceed 5 NTU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recycle notification and reporting requirements (subpart H systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: All subpart H systems that employ conventional or direct filtration and that recycle spent filter backwash, thickener supernatant, or liquids from dewatering processes must notify the State in writing by Dec 8, 2003, if they recycle these flows. Notification must include specific information (plant schematic and flow data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include: a plant schematic showing origin of all recycled flows, hydraulic conveyances, and re-introduction location; typical recycle flow (gpm), highest observed plant flow previous year, design flow for treatment plant, and State-approved operating capacity if determined by State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recycle treatment technique requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that recycle spent filter backwash, thickener supernatant, or dewatering liquids must return these flows through the processes of the system's existing conventional or direct filtration system or at an alternate location approved by the State by June 8, 2004; required capital improvements must be completed by June 8, 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If modifications to recycle location require capital improvements, those improvements must be completed by the deadline to meet treatment process return-location requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recycle recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that recycle must collect and retain on file recycle flow information beginning June 8, 2004, for State review and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records to retain include copy of the recycle notification submitted to State; list of all recycle flows and return frequency; average and maximum backwash flow rate and average/max duration of backwash in minutes; typical filter run length and written summary of how it is determined; type of treatment provided for recycle flow; data on physical dimensions of equalization/treatment units, typical and maximum hydraulic loading rates, type/average dose/frequency of treatment chemicals used, and frequency solids are removed (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability, effective date, and compliance deadlines for Subpart I (lead and copper)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of Subpart I constitute the national primary drinking water regulations for lead and copper and apply to community water systems and non-transient non-community water systems. The subpart is effective as of Dec 30, 2024. Systems must comply with Subpart I no later than Nov 1, 2027, except where otherwise specified or where an exemption under 40 CFR part 142 subpart C or F has been issued. Transitional compliance provisions between Oct 30, 2024 and Nov 1, 2027 specify which codified versions/specific paragraphs apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions issued prior to Dec 16, 2021 may allow systems to comply with an earlier codification until the exemption expires. Specific cross-references to other sections and appendices define transitional compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart I (treatment technique and supporting requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart I is a treatment technique rule including requirements to control corrosion, treat source water, replace service lines, and provide public education, and includes supporting requirements such as a service line inventory, tap sampling, and monitoring for lead in schools/child care facilities. Some requirements apply only if lead/copper action levels are exceeded as measured in tap samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the components of the regulation and when certain elements are triggered by exceedances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead and copper action levels and 90th-percentile calculation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Action levels are determined based on tap water samples considered for inclusion under §141.86(e) and analyzed using methods in §141.89. Lead action level is exceeded if 90th percentile lead concentration > 0.010 mg/L. Copper action level is exceeded if 90th percentile copper concentration > 1.3 mg/L. The 90th percentile concentration must be derived using prescribed ordering, numbering, and selection algorithms that differ depending on whether Tier 1/2 sites exist and whether the minimum number of sites is met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules include: for systems without Tier 1/2 sites, sort all eligible samples ascending, assign ordinal numbers starting at 1, multiply number of samples by 0.9 and select the sample at that position (special averaging for 5-sample case and provisions if <5 samples collected). For systems with sufficient Tier 1/2 sites, include specified sample types (lead: higher of 1L/5L at Tier1/2; copper: all first-liter copper) and follow similar ordering/multiplication rules; for insufficient Tier1/2 sites, combine Tier1/2 higher-valued samples with higher-tier samples to meet minimum site counts, reduce to highest concentrations to meet minimum, then apply ordering and 0.9 multiplication. If insufficient samples overall, calculate 90th percentile per the basic ascending-order-and-multiply-by-0.9 method. Special rules apply when fewer than five samples are collected or the State allows fewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of corrosion control treatment steps by system size
rubrics_metrics.description: All water systems are required to install, optimize, or re-optimize optimal corrosion control treatment (OCCT). This section specifies when systems of different sizes (large >50,000; medium >10,000 ≤50,000; small ≤10,000 and non-transient non-community) must complete corrosion control treatment steps under paragraphs (d) or (e) based on whether they have corrosion control treatment and whether they exceed lead practical quantitation limit, lead action level, and/or copper action level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key size-based rules: systems with corrosion control treatment that exceed lead or copper action levels generally must complete re-optimized OCCT (paragraph d) unless they have already re-optimized once post-compliance-date, are meeting State-designated optimal water quality parameters (OWQPs), and continue to operate/maintain corrosion control treatment; State may require re-optimization in some cases. Systems without corrosion control treatment that exceed thresholds must complete steps to study and install OCCT (paragraph e). Special triggers apply after completing service line replacement if no lead/galvanized-requiring-replacement/unknown lines remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for being deemed to have optimized or re-optimized OCCT
rubrics_metrics.description: A system may be deemed to have OCCT (or re-optimized OCCT) if it meets specified monitoring-performance criteria and documentation requirements and submits documentation to the State by required deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of criteria: A medium system without corrosion control treatment or a small system is deemed to have OCCT if it does not exceed lead and copper action levels during two consecutive six-month tap monitoring periods and then remains ≤ action levels in all subsequent periods (subject to OWQPs). A system is deemed optimized/re-optimized if it demonstrates 90th percentile lead ≤ lead practical quantitation limit (0.005 mg/L) for two consecutive six-month periods, does not exceed copper action level for two consecutive six-month periods, and has no OWQPs designated by the State. Systems deemed to have OCCT must continue monitoring for lead and copper at least once every three calendar years with reduced sites as specified and continue operation/maintenance and any additional State-required measures to ensure OCCT is maintained. If a deemed system later exceeds thresholds, it must follow the required treatment steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 re-optimization requirement: mandatory pipe rig/loop or CCT study and lead service-line harvesting
rubrics_metrics.description: Water systems with corrosion control treatment that are required to re-optimize OCCT must initiate mandatory pipe rig/loop or corrosion control treatment (CCT) study or treatment recommendation. Large or medium water systems with lead service lines that exceed the lead action level must harvest lead service lines from the distribution system and construct flow-through pipe rigs/loops and operate the rigs/loops with finished water within one year after the end of the tap sampling period in which they exceeded the lead action level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This step mandates physical evaluation (harvesting service lines) and bench/field studies (pipe rigs/loops) operated with finished water to inform re-optimization within a one-year deadline.
